passages.note: Leans toward treatment ('done with just putting people away behind bars') while backing Prop 36, which keeps penalties; 'just' does not say 'not punishment', so it does not meet rung 1's absence clause.
In a homelessness answer, supports drug courts and diversion and Prop 36; a pro-treatment lean with no general orientation that excludes punishment or states a case-by-case view.
Calls to prosecute and jail ICE agents who break the law speak to one class of offender in an immigration context, not his general response to lawbreaking.
Recounts an AG prosecution ('Today, he is in jail for his crimes') as a past accomplishment in an answer about rumors and evidence; it names no sentencing orientation.
Sanctuary-state remarks on cooperating with ICE over convicted criminals concern immigration enforcement, not how the system should respond to lawbreaking.

rows.reasoning: Becerra says "Californians are done with just putting people away behind bars" and that drug courts and diversion "must be implemented". Both lean toward support and treatment, but he also backs Prop 36, so neither rules out punishment, as "Focus on support and treatment, not punishment" requires. He states no general case-by-case orientation either, so the evidence shows only a side, not a rung.

quotes.text: Californians are done with just putting people away behind bars.
And so we'd rather have folks who are rehabilitated or who are provided the services they need to stand up again.
And that's where I think these drug courts, these diversion uh programs that we have must be implemented.
I think we should prosecute any of the forces that that violate the law. And I think we should jail anyone who has violated the law.
